title: Micro-demo storm: SE rapid-qualifier deck (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
- One-page, slide-by-slide micro-deck SEs can run in a 6–8 minute live demo to validate fit and surface next-step signals.
- Focus: qualification, latency & cost cues, integration feasibility, and immediate trust-building.

Audience:
- Platform architects, integration leads, and product managers evaluating embedding Redwood inference into a customer workflow.
- Typical ask: prove predictable latency, show basic routing/fallbacks, confirm data isolation options.

High-level flow (6–8 minutes):
1) 30s: Open (Why Redwood matters for cost+latency predictability)
   - Speaker note: Use the customer problem they expressed in discovery (search <customer note>)
   - Quick stat to drop: "Committed capacity reduces latency variance by 40% in our benchmarks" (caller: perf deck)
2) 60s: Live ask + success criteria (what does "pilot success" look like?)
   - Ask: "If we can demonstrate 95th pctl <200ms for your 1k RPS burst and a predictable cost model, is engineering ready to pilot?"
   - Note: capture yes/no as close question.
3) 2m: Live mini-demo (API call -> streaming chunk)
   - Steps: call hosted API with short prompt, show streaming tokens, highlight latency numbers in console, then swap to a fallback (cheaper quantized model) and show seamless failover.
   - Tech checks: have API key, region set to customer region, pre-created model alias (gptx-16k-fast), and a pre-warmed cache snippet ready.
4) 90s: Integration sketch + ops (Trace, cost visibility, rollouts)
   - Show a mock console screenshot with per-route cost, token breakdown, and rollout policy toggle.
   - Note: point out canary + automatic fallback policy.
5) 60s: Objections & quick responses (prep bullets)
   - "Latency risk": show reserved capacity option and SLA
   - "Data residency": explain private deployment & VPC control plane
   - "Cost unpredictability": show Optimize recommendations and prefix caching benefits
6) 30s: Next steps & pilot ask
   - Propose 2-week pilot: 100k tokens/day simulated, 1 endpoint, 1 integration engineer support.

Slide breakdown (titles + speaker cues):
- Slide 1: Title + one-line outcome
  - Cues: keep brand visuals minimal, swap customer logo when allowed
- Slide 2: "Pilot success checklist" (3 bullets)
  - Cues: make forensic checklist — throughput, 95th latency, cost per 1k tokens target
- Slide 3: Live demo frame + what I will show (two quick bullets: streaming + fallback)
- Slide 4: Integration sketch (3 patterns)
  - Pattern A: Direct API calls from backend (typical web app)
  - Pattern B: Edge caching + embedding store (search)
  - Pattern C: Dedicated pool for synchronous low-latency requests
- Slide 5: Ops visibility & rollback knobs
- Slide 6: Pricing anchor + reserved vs burst example (quick math)
- Slide 7: Objection cheat sheet (quick lines to read aloud)
- Slide 8: Immediate next steps and owners

Demo script (practical tips):
- Use a short prompt that aligns with customer domain (have 2 domain templates prepped: customer-support and search-summary).
- Pre-run 3 warmup requests to populate KV cache before live demo shows latency numbers.
- If streaming stalls, switch to a prepared recorded gif — call it out as "network transient" and move on.
- Have a toggle (local) to flip model alias to fallback quantized model to show cost/latency trade.

Rapid-qualifier checklist for SE to collect during demo:
- Business signals: top KPI impacted, allowable latency at 50/95/99 percentiles, and target cost per 1k tokens.
- Technical signals: preferred cloud region, auth method, data residency requirement, whether embeddings/search will be used.
- Operational signals: security reviewer contact, compliance blocker list, expected pilot timeline.

Objection snippets (one-liners SE can read):
- "We can reserve capacity for predictable latency — we have customers who see 2x reduction in 95th pctl variance with reserved pools."
- "If you need air-gapped or VPC-hosted control plane, we offer Private deployment packages with KMS/HSM integrations."
- "Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and batching to lower per-token cost without large quality loss."

Failure modes & recovery script (for live demos):
- Demo API failures: show console logs, call out retry policies, then pivot to a pre-recorded trace demonstrating fallback
- High latency during demo: attribute to warmup/cold start, show reserved capacity numbers and offer follow-up load test within 48 hours
- Customer pushes back on cost: propose a short A/B pilot comparing baseline vs caching/quantization savings and promise a cost estimate within 72 hours

Prep checklist (before meeting):
- Confirm customer's primary region and create model alias matching region naming
- Provision a demo API key scoped to read-only, set usage quota
- Load two warmup prompts into a script, have 3 pre-warm calls set
- Console screenshots: one for per-route cost, one for rollout toggle, one for trace span showing <200ms
- Add meeting to Confluence pilot page and file a Jira ticket to track pilot onboarding (use JIRA-PILOT-874)

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing deck):
- Do we need a variant specifically for ISVs that will embed our SDK? (owner: Miguel)
- Should we include an explicit SLA slide for reserved capacity pricing tiers? (owner: Sasha)
- Can we embed a small interactive latency simulator inside slide 6? feasibility check with design (owner: Jordan)

Measure of success for this enablement asset:
- SEs can run the deck without additional engineering support 70% of the time on first try
- Pilot conversion rate from demo -> paid pilot grows by 15% in Q1 after rollout

Action items (owners):
- Avery: merge final demo script and two domain prompt templates into repo (github link in artifacts) — due 2024-11-21
- Miguel: design 1-page visual for "Pilot success checklist" and supply PNG — due 2024-11-18
- Sasha: draft reserved-capacity SLA language to add to pricing slide — due 2024-11-25

Notes to self / rough fragments (working doc style):
- Keep language very concrete, avoid marketing fluff.
- Need a "quick swap" line for SE to defuse security questions: "We can run a short scribe exchange with your security team next week"
- Consider a variant that is 4-min micro-demo for the 15-min exec slot

Reference material and quick links:
- Perf playbook: confluence.redwood/inference/perf-benchmarks
- Optimize toolkit brief: confluence.redwood/optimize/quick-start
- Demo scripts repo: github.com/redwood-inference/demo-scripts

Revision history (notes):
- 2024-11-07: initial sketch + slide list (Avery)
- 2024-11-12: added demo script / warmup checklist (Miguel)
- 2024-12-05: objection snippets and failure modes expanded (Sasha)
- 2025-01-22: consolidated prep checklist and added owners (Avery)

End of draft.

(Do not finalize until design assets and SLA language land; keeping this intentionally concise for SE readout.)
